lessons.title: Build a Head
lessons.summary: A ball, two lines and a jaw.

steps.title: Ball and jaw
steps.text: Start a head with a ball. Draw a line down the middle of the face (the center line) and a line across where the eyes go (the eye line). Both lines wrap around the ball. Then hang the jaw and chin below.

steps.title: Construct a head
steps.text: Trace the ball, the two wrapping lines and the jaw.
steps.hint: Ball first. Then the curved center line, then the eye line, then the jaw.

quiz.question: What are the two lines that wrap around the head ball?
choices: The center line and the eye line
quiz.explain: They show which way the face is pointing.

lessons.title: Head Turns
lessons.summary: The center line slides around the ball.

steps.title: Turning the head
steps.text: As the head turns, the center line slides across the ball as a curve, and the face rides along with it. Turned all the way to the side, the center line sits right at the edge of the ball.

steps.title: Front to side
steps.text: Draw the head turning: front, three-quarter, then side.
steps.hint: Watch the center line curve more and more.

quiz.question: When the head turns to the side, the center line...
choices: Curves around the ball toward the edge
quiz.explain: It's drawn on the surface of the ball, so it follows the curve.

steps.title: Looking up and down
steps.text: When a head tilts up, the eye line bends upward in the middle like a rainbow. When it tilts down, the eye line bends downward like a smile, and you see more of the top of the head.

steps.title: Looking up
steps.text: Trace the head looking up. The eye line arches like a rainbow.
steps.hint: Ball first, then the arched eye line.

steps.title: Looking down
steps.text: Trace the head looking down. The eye line dips like a smile.
steps.hint: Ball first, then the dipping eye line.

quiz.question: When a character looks down, the eye line curves like...
quiz.explain: Tilting down rolls the middle of the line downward.

lessons.title: Foreshortening
lessons.summary: Things pointing at you look shorter.

steps.title: Pointing at you
steps.text: Foreshortening happens when something points toward you. An arm reaching at the camera looks shorter, and the hand looks much bigger because it's closer. Draw it as overlapping circles: a big one for the hand, smaller ones going back to the shoulder.

steps.title: Reaching arm
steps.text: Trace the arm reaching toward you: three circles joined by straight sides.
steps.hint: Draw the big hand circle first. It overlaps the others.

quiz.question: An arm pointing straight at you looks...
quiz.explain: The length is squashed and the near hand is bigger.
